Let the center of the circular lake be the origin. For any triangle whose vertices are points \(A,B,C\) on this circle, its orthocenter is

\[
H = A+B+C
\]

in vector form.

Take any partition of the 6 points into two triples. If the two triples have orthocenters \(H_1,H_2\), then

\[
H_1+H_2 = \text{(sum of the 3 points in the first triple)} + \text{(sum of the 3 points in the second triple)}
\]

\[
= \text{sum of all 6 pine position vectors}.
\]

Thus the midpoint of the segment joining the two orthocenters is

\[
\frac{H_1+H_2}{2} = \frac12(\text{sum of all 6 pines}),
\]

which is the same fixed point for every possible partition into two triples.

So one dive is enough.

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
